title: Integer Exponents
subtitle: Product, Quotient, Power, Zero, Negative
bounds: PROTOCOL §4b Exponents. Numeric bases 2-10 only (no letters; a missing exponent is a ?). Every exponent in a prompt, a step, a choice or an answer is an integer of size 12 or less, and every exponent step is a signed sum or difference or a times-table product of size 12 or less. Answers stay in power form (2^7) except where a value is asked for: then only a power of 10, 1, the base, or a power of size 100 or less, or 1 over one of these (1/8, 1/100). A negative exponent is written ^−3.

tiers.name: Zero & Negative Powers
tiers.description: Anything to the 0 power is 1. A negative exponent means a reciprocal.

tiers.name: Product Rule
tiers.description: Same base, multiply: add the exponents.

tiers.name: Quotient Rule
tiers.description: Same base, divide: subtract the exponents.

tiers.name: Power of a Power
tiers.description: Raise a power to a power: multiply. Raise a product: each factor gets it.

tiers.name: Mixed Rules to a Value
tiers.description: Use two rules in a row, then find the value.

ZERO_IS_ZERO.student: A 0 exponent doesn't make 0. b^2 ÷ b^2 = 1, and that is b^0.
ZERO_IS_ZERO.teacher: Reads b^0 as 0 (zero exponent means zero).

ZERO_KEEPS_BASE.student: b^0 isn't b. Dividing b^n by b^n gives 1, so b^0 = 1.
ZERO_KEEPS_BASE.teacher: Reads b^0 as b (no multiplications means the base is left alone).

NEG_VALUE.student: A negative exponent doesn't make a negative number. It flips: 2^−3 = 1/8.

NEG_TIMES.student: An exponent counts copies of the base, it isn't a factor. 2^−3 is 1/(2 × 2 × 2).
NEG_TIMES.teacher: Reads b^−n as −(b × n): multiplies base and exponent and keeps the sign.

NEG_FRACTION.student: The minus tells you to flip, not to go negative. 2^−3 = 1/8, a positive.
NEG_FRACTION.teacher: Flips b^−n correctly but keeps a negative sign: −1/b^n.

IGNORE_SIGN.student: The minus matters: 2^−3 is 1/8, not 8. It flips the power.
IGNORE_SIGN.teacher: Drops the sign of the exponent: b^−n = b^n.

TIMES_FOR_POWER.student: An exponent is repeated multiplication, not base × exponent.

RECIP_TIMES.student: Flip the power, don't flip the product. 2^−3 = 1/(2 × 2 × 2) = 1/8.
RECIP_TIMES.teacher: Takes the reciprocal of b × n instead of b^n.

SWAP_BASE_EXP.student: Base and exponent have different jobs. Check which number is the base.
SWAP_BASE_EXP.teacher: Swaps the base and the exponent.

MULT_EXPONENTS.student: Multiplying same-base powers adds the exponents: b^m × b^n = b^(m+n).
MULT_EXPONENTS.teacher: Multiplies the exponents in a product rule step.

MULT_BASES.student: Keep the base the same and add the exponents. The base doesn't change.
MULT_BASES.teacher: Multiplies the bases as well as adding the exponents.

ADD_BASES.student: Keep the base the same and add the exponents. Don't add the bases.
ADD_BASES.teacher: Adds the bases (b + b = 2b) as well as the exponents in a product.

MULT_BOTH.student: Keep the base. Same base: add the exponents. Nothing else changes.
MULT_BOTH.teacher: Multiplies both the bases and the exponents.

SUB_EXPONENTS.student: Multiplying powers adds exponents. Subtracting is for dividing.
SUB_EXPONENTS.teacher: Subtracts the exponents in a product.

SKIPS_FACTOR.student: Use every factor. Add all three exponents.
SKIPS_FACTOR.teacher: Adds only two of the three exponents.

SIGN_SLIP.student: Careful with the minus signs. Add or subtract the signed exponents.
SIGN_SLIP.teacher: Drops a negative sign from an exponent, or flips the sign of the result.

ADD_GIVEN.student: Subtract to find the missing exponent. Added they overshoot.
ADD_GIVEN.teacher: Adds the exponents given instead of undoing the rule with the opposite operation.

COPY_TOTAL.student: The total exponent is the sum (or difference), not the missing one.
COPY_TOTAL.teacher: Gives the exponent of the result as the missing exponent.

MULT_GIVEN.student: Same base: exponents add, so undo it by subtracting, not by multiplying.

DIVIDE_EXPONENTS.student: Dividing same-base powers subtracts exponents: b^m ÷ b^n = b^(m−n).
DIVIDE_EXPONENTS.teacher: Divides the exponents in a quotient rule step.

ADD_EXPONENTS.student: Dividing powers subtracts exponents. Adding is for multiplying.
ADD_EXPONENTS.teacher: Adds the exponents in a quotient.

SUB_NEG.teacher: Adds the exponents in a quotient with a negative divisor exponent: m + n instead of m − n.

DIVIDE_BASES.student: The base stays. Don't divide it: b ÷ b isn't the answer, subtract exponents.
DIVIDE_BASES.teacher: Divides the bases to get 1 as the new base.

FLIPPED_SUB.student: Top exponent minus bottom exponent, in that order. Check the sign.
FLIPPED_SUB.teacher: Subtracts the exponents in the wrong order.

ADD_FOR_POWER.student: A power of a power multiplies the exponents: (b^m)^n = b^(mn).
ADD_FOR_POWER.teacher: Adds the exponents in a power of a power.

DROP_OUTER.student: Use both exponents. The outer one multiplies the inner one.
DROP_OUTER.teacher: Keeps only the inner exponent in a power of a power.

DROP_INNER.student: Use both exponents. The inner one is multiplied by the outer one.
DROP_INNER.teacher: Keeps only the outer exponent in a power of a power.

FIRST_FACTOR_ONLY.student: The exponent goes on every factor inside the parentheses.
FIRST_FACTOR_ONLY.teacher: Applies the exponent to only one factor of a product.

SUM_FOR_PRODUCT.student: A product to a power is a product of powers: (ab)^n = a^n × b^n.
SUM_FOR_PRODUCT.teacher: Replaces the product of powers with a sum.

SUM_BASES.student: The parentheses hold a product, not a sum. Raise each factor.
SUM_BASES.teacher: Adds the bases inside the parentheses instead of keeping them as factors.
